newsitem.title: USA: Federal-Mogul posts $220 million fourth-quarter loss.
newsitem.headline: Federal-Mogul posts $220 million fourth-quarter loss.

text.p: Federal-Mogul Corp. posted a $220 million fourth-quarter loss Thursday and said it had undertaken an "urgent" restructuring that includes cutting 2,900 jobs and taking pre-tax charges of $204 million.
"We are approaching the restructuring with the utmost urgency and expect to be executing our plan throughout 1997," Dick Snell, the company's new chairman and chief executive, said in a statement.

Federal-Mogul, a global manufacturer and distributor of parts for cars, trucks and farm and construction equipment, said it intended to return to profitability by concentrating on manufacturing and abandoning its retailing operations.

"We have realigned our growth strategy behind our core competencies of engineering, manufacturing and distribution," said Snell, who took over in September after Dennis Gormley resigned as chairman and Wayne Smith quit as president.

"Our retail operations are good viable businesses that can be operated better by someone else. We have neither the skills nor the infrastructure necessary to operate and grow them ...," Snell said. "Prompt, decisive action was essential to improve our financial performance."
The company said it lost $220.2 million, or $6.32 a share, in the three months ended Dec. 31, following a loss of $49.1 million, or $1.46 a share, in the same period in 1995.
For all of 1996 Federal-Mogul said it lost $211.1 million, or $6.26 a share, after posting a loss of $9.7 million, or 53 cents a share, in the year earlier.

The company, based in Southfield, Mich., said its sales for the quarter dipped to $480.3 million from $485.1 million while sales for the entire year reached a record $2.03 billion, up from $1.99 billion.

The company said the $204 million restructuring charge includes a write-off of $155 million of impaired goodwill and certain assets and costs associated with restructuring international operations; $13 million for employee severance costs; $22 million for facility closures and consolidations and $14 million for other items.
It said the restructuring actions, which will take most of 1997 to complete, also include a reduction of 2,900 people, or about 18 percent, from a worldwide workforce of 15,700.
The company also said it expected to take further charges in future years to overhaul European manufacturing operations and consolidate warehouse facilities in the United States.
Federal-Mogul's stock added 75 cents to $24.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
